discovery.title: A space telescope that watched cosmic explosions is nearing its fiery return
discovery.summary: NASA’s Swift observatory, launched in 2004 to study gamma-ray bursts, has ended operations and is expected to reenter Earth’s atmosphere in the coming weeks. Most of it is expected to burn up.
discovery.why_it_matters: Swift helped astronomers study some of the universe’s most powerful explosions for more than two decades. Its return is a reminder that space missions eventually become part of Earth’s orbital environment.
